reply.summary: Wrote docs/designs/024-game-slug-identity/01-research.md for ADR-024 (discovered-game slug identity and the 63→128 shared bound). Read set: the ADR plus cited ADRs 013, 021, 022, and the ADR/task directory listings; then 14 files outside that set (discovery slug/game/steam_common/CLI sources and Cargo.toml, core placement/action/lib/error/manifest/policy/document lines, four schema specs, README, three invalid fixtures, discovery slug_tests, rust-toolchain.toml). Findings pin down today's state: one crate-private grammar predicate, four private 63-octet constants (three MAX_SLUG_OCTETS plus a differently named MAX_SEGMENT_OCTETS in action.rs that the ADR's rollout omits), the 63 number restated in four published specs, four Rust test files (not two) that re-pin 63/64, an 'eleven constants' count in schemas/README.md that becomes twelve, no past-cap id fixture in schemas/manifests/v1, and that discovery does not depend on bindforge-core — so 024-L1 forces a new public core API or a duplicate. A survey of 143 live Steam store titles through Valve's store-search endpoint found one title deriving to 64 octets under 024-C2, a byte-identical slug collision between two real store entries, and frequent g- leading-digit cases, but nothing past 128 — so the ADR's 'one octet above the longest surveyed title' basis is unproven. External grounding covers Kubernetes RFC-1123 63-octet labels and its digit-start refusal, UTS #46 IDNA mapping/Punycode, UAX #15 NFKD plus the fact that Rust std has no normalisation API (which collides head-on with the ADR's 'std-only, no transliteration table' clause), Django slugify, WordPress' -2 suffix loop with truncation and _wp_old_slug, FriendlyId history, Steamworks immutable App IDs, IGDB id+slug, git core.protectNTFS with CVE-2019-1353, and NAME_MAX/MAX_PATH/255-character component limits. Eleven open questions are queued for the designer, led by the std-only/NFKD contradiction, the undefined collision-suffix-versus-bound interaction, per-plugin-only collision scope, and Windows reserved device names reachable through derivation.

docs: add design proposal for ADR-024 game slug identity

findings.location: Chosen design → Derivation — "fold precomposed Latin via a private `fold_latin_base(char) -> Option<char>` match table covering Latin-1 Supplement and Latin Extended-A single-base-letter decompositions, both cases"
findings.problem: The steps are stated "in order" with ASCII case-fold first and the Latin fold second, and the Options section says each covered letter "maps to that base", meaning its Unicode canonical-decomposition base. For every uppercase precomposed letter that base is ASCII uppercase (Å → A, É → E, İ → I), and the ASCII case-fold has already run behind it, so the next clause — "map every remaining character outside `[a-z0-9]` to `-`" — dashes it out. `Åpen` derives `pen`; an accented all-caps title loses every accented letter. That is precisely the accented-folds-to-`-` loss the Options section cites as the reason to keep the diacritic clause ("\"Pokémon\" → `pok-mon`"). Test strategy #1 cannot catch it: its diacritic cases (é, ü, ñ) are all lowercase, and A15's registered claim is about the fold reproducing NFKD, not about case.
findings.fix: One clause: the table maps each covered letter to its lower-case ASCII base (or the ASCII case-fold is re-applied after the diacritic fold); add an upper-case accented case (É → e, Å → a) to Test strategy #1.

findings.location: Chosen design → Specs, fixtures, ledger — "the four `spec.md` sentences (A3) are amended in place: the number and the RFC 1035 derivation are replaced by a cross-reference"
findings.problem: A3's action-ids citation is `schemas/action-ids/v1/spec.md:54` only, so line 58 of the same sentence is left unamended: "`move..steer`, `steer-left`, `move.steer.left`, and a 64-octet segment are each a refusal, and each has a fixture under `fixtures/invalid/` naming it". Under `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS = 128` a 64-octet segment is legal, so the amended published spec refuses something two lines above it now permits, and the fixture it promises to name is the file this run renames to `segment-past-cap.toml` with a 129-octet segment.
findings.fix: Extend the amendment list and A3's citation to that example clause: replace "a 64-octet segment" with "a segment past the shared bound" so it names the renamed fixture instead of a stale length.

findings.location: Test strategy #6 — "`crates/core/tests/{manifest.rs, policy.rs, chain_ops.rs, action.rs}` accept 128 and refuse 129"
findings.problem: Those four are exactly the files pinning the 63/64 boundary, but the file pinning the action-ids invalid fixture's *name* is a fifth: `crates/core/tests/action_ids.rs:124` lists `"segment-past-63-octets.toml"` in its required-fixture set. Neither Test strategy #6 nor #10 names it, so the fixture rename this design orders has no named re-pin site.
findings.fix: Add `action_ids.rs` (with the new literal `segment-past-cap.toml`) to #6's file list and to Rollout item 1's re-pin list.

findings.location: Chosen design → Emission, refusal and collisions — "refusals increment the existing `skipped` counter, and that diagnostic's wording widens from \"unreadable or malformed\" to name un-derivable names as well"
findings.problem: That diagnostic is `crates/discovery/src/steam_common.rs:101`, guarded by `!self.roots.is_empty() && games.is_empty() && skipped > 0`: it fires only when the plugin emitted nothing. A scan that refuses one game and emits the rest prints nothing, so the widened wording never appears in the ordinary mixed case, and 024-L1's "a violation is a named refusal" is user-invisible for the Steam plugins — their rows are refused inside the plugin and never reach the CLI's named `error: refused game with invalid slug:` line.
findings.fix: Emit one named line per construction-path refusal through `escape_and_truncate` (mirroring the CLI's line, no path), or state that plugin-side refusals are count-only and that 024-L1's named refusal is the CLI-boundary line alone.

findings.location: Chosen design → Identity shape — "`pub enum Namespace { Unknown }` with `#[serde(rename_all = \"kebab-case\")]` and a `Display` impl, mirroring `Platform`'s pattern"
findings.problem: The pattern cited does not exist: `Platform` (`crates/discovery/src/game.rs:5-18`) carries no serde attribute, and `apps/discovery-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs:186-189` pins `obj["platform"] == "SteamLinux"` with the comment that "the r1 major `#[serde(rename_all = \"kebab-case\")]` was reverted as unauthorized". A builder following the cited precedent emits `"Unknown"` against a value pinned to `"unknown"` in three places, and the JSON row ends up mixing `"namespace":"unknown"` with `"platform":"SteamLinux"` without that being a stated, deliberate divergence.
findings.fix: Delete "mirroring `Platform`'s pattern" and state the deliberate divergence from it (and that the closed-enum JSON spelling in this row is now mixed).

findings.location: Chosen design → Shared grammar and bound ("surveyed-title rationale per ADR-024, with A16's caveat") vs Specs, fixtures, ledger ("with the substituted rationale")
findings.problem: The same constant is given two different published rationales; the README is 024-L3's one stated home, so its wording is the contract while the code doc comment cites a clause the README drops.
findings.fix: Write the rationale once and reuse it in both places, stating whether 024-B1's "one octet above the longest surveyed store display title" clause is carried (with A16's caveat) or replaced.

findings.location: Rollout item 2 — "Same commit as the constant bump so code and spec text cannot drift (024-L3)"
findings.problem: Commit-level atomicity is required for constant-plus-specs, yet item 4 (discovery, including "the eight re-pinned test files", four of which live in `apps/discovery-cli/tests/`) is sequenced ahead of item 5 (the CLI's `Namespace` column and JSON shape), so no intermediate commit satisfies `cargo test --workspace --locked`.
findings.fix: One clause: items 4 and 5 land as one commit, or state that the gates are branch-level and only items 1+2 are commit-atomic.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Third-party schema readers | Unknown | Built against the 63-octet text they refuse 64–128-octet ids until they re-read the amended specs"
findings.problem: A compatibility-matrix row whose status is `unknown` is a major finding under checklist item 1; the row commits to no status. The proposal's own material permits a commitment: 024-L3 makes the amendment relaxation-only (documents valid under the 63-octet text stay valid at 128) and A7 shows no shipped document exceeds 63 today, so every known artifact is accepted by both old-text and new-text readers; divergence is confined to future ids no known consumer produces.
findings.fix: Replace the "Unknown" status with a definite one — e.g. "Yes, with a known behaviour change" — and keep the existing note: old-text readers reject only 64–128-octet ids, of which zero ship at merge. That is a committed status replacing an uncommitted one; the mitigations stay unchanged.

findings.location: Test strategy #11 — "Platform: the whole suite runs unchanged on the Linux and Windows CI matrix" (with matrix rows Windows "Yes, with named gaps" and macOS "Yes")
findings.problem: The named CI matrix does not exist and nothing in the run creates it: every job in the repo's workflows runs ubuntu-latest (check.yml `rust` and `orchestration` jobs; advisories.yml), and the Windows leg of the gate is a cross-compile `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` that performs no code generation or linking — no test binary ever runs on Windows. Rollout item 7 pins the gates per `.github/workflows/check.yml` and no rollout item adds a Windows runner, so the Windows platform test is unexecutable as written and the Windows "Yes" support claim carries no runtime verification. Checklist item 7 fails again for macOS: the matrix claims "Yes" but no Test strategy item names a macOS platform test.
findings.fix: One of two edits: (a) add `windows-latest` (and `macos-latest`, if the Yes claims stand) legs to check.yml as a named rollout item and keep #11's wording; or (b) rewrite #11 to the real gate — full suite on Linux, Windows compile-verified via the existing MSVC `cargo check` leg, derivation/collision/refusal outcomes platform-independent — and downgrade the Windows and macOS matrix rows' statuses to that verification level.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "`tools/orchestration` (Node) | Not affected | No slug-grammar surface there"
findings.problem: The stated basis is false as written: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/types.ts:287 defines `SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`, the pipeline-internal run-identity `nnn-slug` grammar. The "Not affected" conclusion holds (distinct grammar that admits a leading digit, rides no shared product slug bound, reads nothing in the changed surface), but anyone grepping "slug" in that package will find the constant and read the row's basis as refuted.
findings.fix: Restate the row's basis as: "the pipeline-internal `nnn-slug` run-identity grammar is a distinct grammar that rides no shared product slug bound; no code there reads the changed surface".

findings.location: CLI boundary and output — "dropped, with one stderr line `error: refused game with invalid slug: <escape_and_truncate(value)>` and no path (024-L1)"
findings.problem: "and no path" overstates the mechanism if read as "no path-shaped text can appear on this line": escape_and_truncate (verified crates/core/src/error.rs:172-186) escapes control characters and truncates at 80 chars but passes '/' and '.' through, so a hostile plugin that puts path-shaped text in the slug field has that text echoed back (escaped, bounded). The guarantees actually provided are: single-line, bounded, escaped echo of the plugin's own value, and no install path emitted by the CLI.
findings.fix: Reword the clause to "and no CLI-sourced path; the echo is the escaped, length-bounded value only" — one sentence, no new mechanism.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Emission, refusal and collisions — `crates/discovery`", read with the Risks row "Collision-suffix probe loop repeats bound checks many times" — "probe count is bounded by distinct-name count, no measurable cost today"
findings.problem: The stated bound is per name, not per run. As specified, every colliding name restarts its probe at `base-2` and walks the claimed set, so n distinct display names sharing one base cost about n^2/2 candidate constructions, each a fresh String plus an is_slug_name and bound check. Nothing in the design caps rows a plugin may return — unlike the sibling budgets the new constant joins (MAX_MANIFEST_ROWS = 256 et al.) — so the multiplier is whatever the host's appmanifest_*.acf count is. Minor because this is a hand-run bulk CLI scan, never an event path (no event/keystroke path exists in the tree; the only binary is apps/discovery-cli), and realistic n keeps the term invisible.
findings.fix: Replace the row's mitigation with the honest shape — aggregate probes are O(n^2) in one plugin run's distinct-name count, n bounded only by the host's manifest-file count — or store a next-free-suffix counter on each base entry of the assigned-slug map so a collision consumes one candidate instead of rescanning claimed ones, making the pass linear. Either keeps one mechanism and adds no constant.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Specs, fixtures, ledger" — "`schemas/README.md` gains the bound's one stated home, a bullet in the exported budget family: `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS = 128`"
findings.problem: Every existing entry in that family (schemas/README.md:99-125) carries an explicit aggregate-cost clause: ADR-013's ends "the shared 1 MiB / 16-deep budgets still bind first", ADR-014's states "adds no aggregate cap … MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (32 MiB)", ADR-015's gives 64 × 16 predicate moves. The design specifies the bullet's rationale, the RFC 1035 supersession sentence and the eleven→twelve fix, but no composition clause — even though this entry doubles an existing bound on values that appear inside every capped array that adversarial-guard section governs.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the bullet in ADR-013's words: the doubling adds no aggregate byte ceiling because MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES / MAX_NESTING_DEPTH still bind first. No new mechanism, one sentence in the stated home.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Derivation — `crates/discovery/src/slug.rs`" — "ASCII case-fold (`A-Z`→`a-z`); fold precomposed Latin via a private `fold_latin_base` …; map every remaining character outside `[a-z0-9]` to `-`; collapse `-` runs; trim `-` at both ends; prefix a leading digit with `g-`"
findings.problem: Read as steps, this is five to six full-string passes over input no field-level cap constrains: read_text_file caps an ACF at 1 MiB (steam_common.rs:282) but not the `name` value inside it, and the bound is deliberately applied only after the whole slug exists ("Length is **not** truncated anywhere"). Today's normalize_slug already allocates four intermediate Strings per name (crates/discovery/src/slug.rs:1-35), so this is not a regression — but the canonical rewrite is the moment to pin the shape.
findings.fix: One clause: derive_slug folds case, folds Latin, maps, and collapses runs in a single char loop into one String builder, with trim and the `g-` prefix done as slices/prepend rather than rewrites, so a name of any length costs one buffer.

reply.summary: All ten open findings consumed by changing the design, not appending: Derivation now folds precomposed Latin to its lower-case ASCII base before the ASCII case-fold (Options (c) and Test strategy #1 follow, so `Åpen`→`apen`); the action-ids spec amendment covers the refusal-example clause ("a 64-octet segment"→"a segment past the shared bound", A3 extended to :58) and names `action_ids.rs` as the fixture-literal re-pin site in Test strategy #6 and Rollout 1; plugin-side refusals are now stated as count-only into `skipped` (whose message only fires when nothing was emitted, steam_common.rs:101), leaving 024-L1's named refusal to the CLI boundary, and the Goals echo line was reverted rather than reworded; Identity shape drops the false `Platform` serde precedent and states the deliberate divergence from the pinned `"SteamLinux"`; the bound's rationale exists once, in the README bullet, with `placement.rs` copying it and 024-B1's surveyed-title clause replaced, not repeated (A16); Rollout states commit granularity (items 1+2, items 4+5 one commit, rest branch-level), replacing the stale same-commit clause; Test strategy #11 and the Windows/macOS matrix rows now describe the real gate (Linux suite, Windows cross-compile check, no macOS leg), the third-party-schema-reader row commits to "Yes, with a known behaviour change" (relaxation-only, zero >63 ids at merge), and the orchestration row cites the distinct pipeline-internal `SLUG_RE` grammar as its basis; deletions paid for the placement.rs duplicate rationale, the item-2 commit clause and a trimmed initial log entry, and the diff is net positive (+27) because ten findings across nine sections each required a substantive rewrite while only two passages were removable outright.

findings.location: Chosen design → Emission, refusal and collisions — "they increment the existing `skipped` counter (whose message counts files, so a refused row counts there as a skipped row)"
findings.problem: The count-only closure is accepted, but the new parenthetical bakes in a conflation that misreports in the one case the counter is ever user-visible: the counter's only surface is the steam_common.rs:101 error, whose message reads "N file(s) skipped as unreadable or malformed". When every game a plugin finds is refused for an un-derivable name — exactly the case ADR-024's Consequences foresee ("a game whose display name and install directory are both non-Latin gets refused at discovery") — the diagnostic fires and attributes readable, well-formed files to "unreadable or malformed", naming neither a game nor the actual cause.
findings.fix: In this bullet, split the fired message's counts (e.g. "M file(s) skipped as unreadable or malformed; K game(s) refused") or drop the "unreadable or malformed" attribution from the combined count.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Emission, refusal and collisions — `crates/discovery`", read with the unchanged Risks row "Collision-suffix probe loop repeats bound checks many times" — "probe count is bounded by distinct-name count, no measurable cost today"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1, unaddressed and unrebutted by the Revision log; the c2 diff did not touch this section's collision pass. The bound is per name, not per run: each colliding name restarts at `base-2` and walks the claimed set, so n distinct display names sharing one base cost roughly n^2/2 candidate constructions, each a fresh String plus an is_slug_name and bound check. `crates/discovery` carries only MAX_FILE_BYTES = keyvalues::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (steam_common.rs:282), a whole-file cap, and the design caps no plugin row count, so the multiplier is the host's appmanifest_*.acf count. Minor, because this stays a hand-run bulk CLI scan (the only binary is apps/discovery-cli; no event path exists) and realistic n keeps the term invisible.
findings.fix: Replace the row's mitigation with the honest shape — aggregate probes are O(n^2) in one plugin run's distinct-name count, n bounded only by the host's manifest-file count — or store a next-free-suffix counter on each base entry of the assigned-slug map so a collision consumes one candidate instead of rescanning claimed ones. Either keeps one mechanism and adds no constant.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Specs, fixtures, ledger" — "a bullet in the exported budget family, `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS = 128`, the shared bound for every slug-grammar id; sibling of `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS` (A8) …"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1; the revised bullet still specifies no aggregate-cost clause, although every neighbouring entry in that family carries one (schemas/README.md: "the shared 1 MiB / 16-deep budgets still bind first"; MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES; 64 × 16 predicate moves). This entry doubles an existing bound on values appearing inside arrays those budgets govern. One c2 revision widens the gap: the bullet is now "the single rationale text that `placement.rs`'s doc comment copies verbatim", so the omission propagates from the README into the exported constant's documentation in code.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the bullet in ADR-013's words: the doubling adds no aggregate byte ceiling because MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES / MAX_NESTING_DEPTH still bind first. One sentence in the stated home, no new mechanism.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Derivation — `crates/discovery/src/slug.rs`" — "in order: fold precomposed Latin via a private `fold_latin_base(char) -> Option<char>` match table … then ASCII case-fold (`A-Z`→`a-z`); then map every remaining character outside `[a-z0-9]` to `-`; collapse `-` runs; trim `-` at both ends; prefix a leading digit with `g-`"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1; the c2 reorder (Latin table before case-fold, lower-case bases) is cost-neutral — the table is a compile-time char match consulted once per char either way — but the step list is still readable as five to six full-string passes over input no field-level cap constrains, with the bound applied only after the whole slug exists ("Length is **not** truncated anywhere"). Not a regression: today's normalize_slug already allocates four intermediate Strings per name.
findings.fix: One clause: derive_slug folds Latin, folds case, maps, and collapses runs in a single char loop into one String builder, with trim and the `g-` prefix done as slices/prepend rather than rewrites, so a name of any length costs one buffer.

findings.location: docs/adrs/013-game-manifests.md:114 (file absent from the diff range)
findings.problem: The proposal's Goals, its 'Specs, fixtures, ledger' section, and ADR-024 Rollout 5 require the `013-L5` unit line to gain an `amended-by 024-B1` annotation per `021-L4`. The branch never touches `docs/adrs/013-game-manifests.md`, and at HEAD the 013-L5 line carries no `amended-by` annotation. A branch that raises the shared bound and amends four published contracts would merge with the amended unit's ledger row un-annotated; no gate test reads the ledger, so nothing else forces this to land.
findings.fix: Append the `amended-by 024-B1` annotation to the `013-L5` unit line in `docs/adrs/013-game-manifests.md` so it is inside the run's diff range (013's prose and `013-R1` untouched). If `docs/adrs/` is outside the build stage's ownership, the runner — which owns these commits per the proposal — must make the edit part of this run before completion.

findings.location: schemas/action-ids/v1/spec.md:54; schemas/policy/v1/spec.md:40 and ~:92; schemas/manifests/v1/spec.md:54; schemas/profile/v2/spec.md:38 and :71
findings.problem: The proposal mandates that in the four amended specs 'the number and the RFC 1035 derivation become a cross-reference to the README bullet' — 024-L3: 'cross-references it instead of restating the number' — and the new README bullet (copied verbatim into placement.rs's doc comment) asserts the four 'now cross-reference this bullet instead of carrying a number of its own'. All four specs still publish the literal: 'at most `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS` = 128 octets'. The README/placement claim is false against the shipped corpus, and a future bound amendment would leave four published '128' literals to rot — the constant drift 024-B1's one-stated-home rule exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Drop the `= 128` gloss from all six sentences, e.g. 'at most `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS` octets — the shared bound `schemas/README.md` states once (`024-B1`)'. The profile/v2 `derives` row in this same diff already uses the number-free form.

findings.location: crates/core/src/action.rs:38-56 and :257-277; crates/core/src/document.rs:1259-1265; crates/core/src/manifest.rs:538-543
findings.problem: The proposal's only mandate for these refusal messages was that strings embedding the number be built with `format!` from the exported constant. The implementation also restructures core's public InvalidValue message shapes: `SEGMENT_EDGE_RULE` folded into a reworded `SEGMENT_SHAPE_RULE`, `invalid_id`'s echo moved from leading to trailing position, a new `segment_bound_rule`/`invalid_segment` split, and bound-refusal messages reordered to lead with the number. Accepted/rejected sets are unchanged and the new shapes are pinned by tests, but the change to the rejection-text surface is wider than the design asked for.
findings.fix: No code change sought: record the message-order restructure as a declared deviation in `03-build-notes.md` if it is not already recorded there.

findings.location: apps/discovery-cli/tests/cli_slug_refusal_tests.rs:33 (`const SLUG_BOUND: usize = 128`), :113 (`fn is_slug_shaped`), :25-26 (justifying note)
findings.problem: The CLI-side boundary pin retypes the shared bound as a file-local constant and re-implements the slug grammar by hand, on the stated premise that the crate's tests have no bindforge-core dependency. That premise is false in this change: apps/discovery-cli/Cargo.toml:8-11 adds `bindforge-core = { workspace = true }`, and a package's [dependencies] are available to its tests/ targets — the same route crates/discovery/tests/slug_tests.rs:23 and game_tests.rs:131-140 already use for `bindforge_core::{MAX_SLUG_OCTETS, is_slug_name}`. The pin that proves 'every slug reaching a rendering is inside the shared bound' therefore asserts a number production no longer reads (main.rs:89-96 reads the constant), so the next bound amendment — the event 024-L3 explicitly plans for — leaves this conformance-style pin enforcing 128 while the CLI enforces the new value; the hand-rolled predicate drifts the same way and is a second grammar in the tree, which the proposal's Options section rejected for discovery.
findings.fix: Delete SLUG_BOUND and is_slug_shaped and assert against bindforge_core::MAX_SLUG_OCTETS and bindforge_core::is_slug_name, as the discovery suites do; remove the note that justifies the copy.

findings.location: apps/discovery-cli/tests/cli_slug_refusal_tests.rs:258 and :328
findings.problem: Both assertions hard-code the Linux answer to a cfg-dependent choice: apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:58-65 feeds --steam-root to SteamLinuxPlugin on non-Windows and SteamWindowsPlugin on Windows, so the expected `error: plugin steam-linux failed: ` prefix and the `steam-linux` Platform cell are platform-specific outcomes, while Test strategy #11 states no test asserts a platform-specific outcome. Nothing breaks in today's CI (no Windows or macOS test leg), so this is a forward hazard for the verification level the matrix's Windows row eventually wants, and it follows the pre-existing pattern in cli_tests.rs rather than introducing one.
findings.fix: Derive the expected plugin name (or accept either spelling) and note in the file header that these two assertions ride the Linux leg only.

findings.location: crates/discovery/src/slug.rs:19
findings.problem: The fold table's coverage comment lists `ł` twice in its stroke-letter sample — (`ł`, `đ`, `ħ`, `ŧ`, `ł`) — where the fifth entry was presumably `ŀ` (U+0140) or `Ł` (U+0141). That comment is the stated coverage boundary Test strategy #1 pins, so its sample set should name the real code points; the match ranges themselves are correct.
findings.fix: Correct the duplicated code point in the doc comment.

findings.location: apps/discovery-cli/src/main.rs:88-102 (CLI emit-boundary filter and `error: refused game with invalid slug:` echo); Test strategy #9 at docs/designs/024-game-slug-identity/02-proposal.md:288-290
findings.problem: Test strategy #9 promises that a plugin row violating the grammar or bound is dropped by the CLI "with one named stderr refusal containing the escaped echo, while valid rows still render". No test asserts that behaviour at any layer. Every CLI test in cli_slug_refusal_tests.rs (138, 181, 233) drives the binary through scratch Steam roots, so the row is refused earlier inside steam_common::discovered_game and never reaches main.rs's new filter; the file's own header (cli_slug_refusal_tests.rs:5-19) states the injection seam does not exist because the binary builds its own two plugins. findings.location: Chosen design → Emission, refusal and collisions — "they increment the existing `skipped` counter (whose message counts files, so a refused row counts there as a skipped row)"
findings.problem: The count-only closure is accepted, but the new parenthetical bakes in a conflation that misreports in the one case the counter is ever user-visible: the counter's only surface is the steam_common.rs:101 error, whose message reads "N file(s) skipped as unreadable or malformed". When every game a plugin finds is refused for an un-derivable name — exactly the case ADR-024's Consequences foresee ("a game whose display name and install directory are both non-Latin gets refused at discovery") — the diagnostic fires and attributes readable, well-formed files to "unreadable or malformed", naming neither a game nor the actual cause.
findings.fix: In this bullet, split the fired message's counts (e.g. "M file(s) skipped as unreadable or malformed; K game(s) refused") or drop the "unreadable or malformed" attribution from the combined count.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Emission, refusal and collisions — `crates/discovery`", read with the unchanged Risks row "Collision-suffix probe loop repeats bound checks many times" — "probe count is bounded by distinct-name count, no measurable cost today"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1, unaddressed and unrebutted by the Revision log; the c2 diff did not touch this section's collision pass. The bound is per name, not per run: each colliding name restarts at `base-2` and walks the claimed set, so n distinct display names sharing one base cost roughly n^2/2 candidate constructions, each a fresh String plus an is_slug_name and bound check. `crates/discovery` carries only MAX_FILE_BYTES = keyvalues::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (steam_common.rs:282), a whole-file cap, and the design caps no plugin row count, so the multiplier is the host's appmanifest_*.acf count. Minor, because this stays a hand-run bulk CLI scan (the only binary is apps/discovery-cli; no event path exists) and realistic n keeps the term invisible.
findings.fix: Replace the row's mitigation with the honest shape — aggregate probes are O(n^2) in one plugin run's distinct-name count, n bounded only by the host's manifest-file count — or store a next-free-suffix counter on each base entry of the assigned-slug map so a collision consumes one candidate instead of rescanning claimed ones. Either keeps one mechanism and adds no constant.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Specs, fixtures, ledger" — "a bullet in the exported budget family, `MAX_SLUG_OCTETS = 128`, the shared bound for every slug-grammar id; sibling of `MAX_NATIVE_NAME_OCTETS` (A8) …"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1; the revised bullet still specifies no aggregate-cost clause, although every neighbouring entry in that family carries one (schemas/README.md: "the shared 1 MiB / 16-deep budgets still bind first"; MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES; 64 × 16 predicate moves). This entry doubles an existing bound on values appearing inside arrays those budgets govern. One c2 revision widens the gap: the bullet is now "the single rationale text that `placement.rs`'s doc comment copies verbatim", so the omission propagates from the README into the exported constant's documentation in code.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the bullet in ADR-013's words: the doubling adds no aggregate byte ceiling because MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES / MAX_NESTING_DEPTH still bind first. One sentence in the stated home, no new mechanism.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Derivation — `crates/discovery/src/slug.rs`" — "in order: fold precomposed Latin via a private `fold_latin_base(char) -> Option<char>` match table … then ASCII case-fold (`A-Z`→`a-z`); then map every remaining character outside `[a-z0-9]` to `-`; collapse `-` runs; trim `-` at both ends; prefix a leading digit with `g-`"
findings.problem: re-raised from r1; the c2 reorder (Latin table before case-fold, lower-case bases) is cost-neutral — the table is a compile-time char match consulted once per char either way — but the step list is still readable as five to six full-string passes over input no field-level cap constrains, with the bound applied only after the whole slug exists ("Length is **not** truncated anywhere"). Not a regression: today's normalize_slug already allocates four intermediate Strings per name.
findings.fix: One clause: derive_slug folds Latin, folds case, maps, and collapses runs in a single char loop into one String builder, with trim and the `g-` prefix done as slices/prepend rather than rewrites, so a name of any length costs one buffer.
